samples.claim: Private x86 module contains check_flag(x:usize,position:u32)->bool and pub-in-private-module has_avx512_f16_support()/has_avx512(). FP16 detection first requires has_avx512(), then uses unsafe __cpuid(7) and tests EDX bit 23; has_avx512 uses is_x86_feature_detected!(avx512f). The CPUID instruction is architecture-gated and the feature gate precedes the raw bit test; downstream kernel safety still depends on callers. allow(unused_unsafe) accommodates toolchains differing on intrinsic safety. External links are comments, not fetched evidence. These helpers are not publicly reachable through the private module.
samples.review_note: Matches architecture cfg, private module, AVX512 prerequisite, CPUID EDX bit23 and safety-compatibility annotation.

These are format/documented IO layout expectations rather than proof a particular backend uses direct IO.

samples.claim: Default remap_row_ids(&self,&[u64])->Result<Vec<Option<u64>>> reserves input length, iterates in input order and sequentially awaits remap_row_id, pushing one result per input. Duplicates and None positions are preserved, empty input gives empty Vec, and the first Err stops iteration and discards the partial result. There is no concurrent buffering or aggregation. Cancellation can interrupt an in-flight single-row future; the trait makes no rollback promise for implementation side effects.
samples.review_note: Matches sequential await, order/duplicates/None preservation and ? short-circuit; cancellation/rollback limits are explicit deductions.

samples.claim: Fallible library paths return contextual Result errors rather than panics/unwraps; use NotSupported instead of TODO/unimplemented, classify errors by cause, checked arithmetic for IDs/counters, debug assertions for non-safety invariants, and explicit handling of impossible states. A subsequent narrower rule permits expect with a reason only when unavoidable; this is not encouragement to bypass the earlier fallible-path prohibition. Warn for cleanup failures/silent no-ops, avoid duplicate warning-before-error, reject missing required config rather than defaulting, and advance/bind parallel iterators exactly once before skipping work.
samples.evidence:
41 | ## Error Handling
42 | 
43 | - Never use `.unwrap()`, `.expect()`, `panic!()`, or `assert!()` in library code for fallible operations — use `?` with `Result` and proper error types. Reserve `.unwrap()` for tests only.
44 | - Avoid bare `.unwrap()`; use `if let`, `match`, `let ... else`, `?`, or combinators. Never `.is_none()` followed by `.unwrap()`. If unavoidable, use `.expect("reason")`.
45 | - Return `LanceError::NotSupported` instead of `todo!()` or `unimplemented!()` for unsupported code paths. Test with `Result::Err` assertions, not `#[should_panic]`.
46 | - Match `Error` variant to root cause: `Error::invalid_input` for caller data issues, `Error::corrupt_file` for format/integrity issues, `Error::not_found` for missing resources, `Error::io` for I/O failures.
47 | - Include full context in error messages — variable names, values, sizes, types, indices. Not generic messages like `"Invalid chunk size"`.
48 | - Use `checked_add`/`checked_mul` instead of `wrapping_add`/`wrapping_mul` for counters and IDs — return an error on overflow.
49 | - Prefer `debug_assert!` over `assert!` for non-safety invariants; reserve `assert!` for conditions preventing data corruption. Always include descriptive messages.
50 | - Don't silently guard against impossible conditions — use `debug_assert!`, return an explicit error, or remove the check.
51 | - Log warnings on best-effort/cleanup failures instead of silently swallowing or propagating errors.
52 | - Log warnings for silent no-ops (skipped operations); omit warnings before errors since the error message is sufficient.
53 | - Avoid `unwrap_or(default)` on map lookups for required config params — use `.ok_or_else(|| Error::...)` and verify key names match between serialization and deserialization.
54 | - Advance all parallel iterators before any `continue` branches — early exits that skip `.next()` calls cause misalignment.
55 | - Bind `iter.next()` with `let Some(x) = iter.next() else { ... }` — never call `.next()` twice to check-then-use.
56 |
samples.review_note: Matches all error-policy bullets, preserving the narrower expect qualification.

samples.claim: Ready(None) marks exhausted and clears polling. Ready(Some(item)) also clears polling, then checks whether the opposite side is alive: if alive, forget the acquired permit, increment the peer's u32 counter and enqueue item.clone(); if dropped, skip clone/counter/queue and let the permit release normally. The original item goes directly to the polling side. A clone panic happens while holding the state mutex after permit/counter updates, so poisoning/recovery is not handled here. Unbounded queued counts still use u32, so capacity-independent integer overflow is possible at extreme backlog; no runtime reproduction is claimed.
samples.review_note: Matches readiness/peer/permit/counter/clone order; additionally read lock reacquisition at 184-195 and original-result return at 225-246. Add these cross-range citations for tighter claim traceability.

samples.claim: Nested WriterVersion stores library string=1, version string=2, optional prerelease string=3, optional build_metadata string=4. Version is a string because library versions may not be semver; semver has no leading v. New manifests should store core major.minor.patch in version and separate prerelease/build to remain parseable by older readers. Absent prerelease leaves version as-is, absent build means none. Manifest.writer_version=13 enables detection of files affected by writer-specific bugs; this is not itself a file-format gate.
